basis: Skin fragility and pyloric atresia define disease; urinary abnormalities 30-79%; microtia 3/3 represents auricular hypoplasia. Muscular dystrophy 5-29% excluded.

decisions.otologic: involved: microtia in 3/3 is a persistent structural deficiency of the external ear.

basis: Motor-neuron degeneration with possible frontotemporal dementia; muscle wasting and respiratory weakness reflect denervation, without intrinsic muscle or lung disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: weakness and atrophy arise from motor-neuron loss; intrinsic skeletal-muscle damage is not established.

basis: Microcephaly, seizures and developmental impairment define disease; strabismus 2/2. Renal ultrasound changes in 1/2 lack established damaging pathology or functional impairment.

decisions.renal: none: echogenicity and reduced corticomedullary differentiation in 1/2 do not establish damaging renal disease or functional impairment.

basis: Central/peripheral axonopathy; persistent tendon abnormalities 80-99% and skeletal deformities 30-79% support musculoskeletal involvement. Hair morphology lacks demonstrated functional damage.

decisions.dermatologic: none: pili canaliculi and woolly hair are characteristic morphology without demonstrated loss of hair or skin function.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: tendon abnormalities occur in 80-99%, with persistent scoliosis and foot deformities in 30-79%, supporting structural involvement.

basis: Defining enteropathy, hepatic fibrosis 14/27 and immunodeficiency 11/12; neurodevelopmental delay 10/16 (~63%). Hair-shaft disease 22/22 omitted at cap in favor of more severe organ dysfunction.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatic disease is named and defining; fibrosis occurs in 14/27 (~52%).
decisions.neurologic: involved: neurodevelopmental impairment occurs in 10/16 (~63%); retained for its functional severity.
decisions.dermatologic: none: defining hair-shaft defects occur in 22/22, but are omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of enteropathy, immunodeficiency, hepatic fibrosis and neurodevelopmental impairment.

basis: Craniosynostosis, hearing impairment 69/89 and developmental delay 63/95 are defining features. Strabismus occurs in 31/69 (~45%).

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental delay is explicitly part of the syndrome definition and occurs in 63/95 (~66%).
decisions.otologic: primary: hearing loss is explicitly part of the syndrome definition and occurs in 69/89 (~78%).

basis: Cutaneous lupus, cytopenias and chorea each 1/3; AQP4-associated disease excluded. Oral ulcers and mitral regurgitation, each 1/3, omitted at cap; arthralgia alone insufficient.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: oral ulcers occur in 1/3 and qualify, but are omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of more consequential skin, blood and neurologic involvement.
decisions.neurologic: involved: lupus-associated chorea occurs in 1/3, meeting the frequency threshold independently of separately diagnosed AQP4-associated myelitis/optic neuritis.

basis: Immunodeficiency with defining hepatic dysfunction (100%) and encephalopathy/seizures (4/4). Functional hyposplenia is supported by Howell-Jolly bodies in 2/2; cardiac defects individually 1/4.

decisions.hepatic: primary: recurrent hepatopathy, fibrosis and hepatic dysfunction are defining features; decreased liver function is obligate.
decisions.neurologic: primary: recurrent encephalopathy and difficult-to-control seizures are defining features, present in 4/4; cerebral atrophy occurs in 3/3.

basis: Joubert neurodevelopmental disorder; retinal dystrophy 4/4 and finger contractures 2/4 support involvement. Renal and cardiac malformations each 1/8 are below threshold.

decisions.ocular: involved: retinal dystrophy damages the retina in 4/4; the supplied definition and ancestry establish a neurologic syndrome rather than a defining ocular disease.

basis: Cardiac, ectodermal and neurodevelopmental abnormalities define CFC. Ocular dysfunction, including strabismus and refractive errors, affects >30% across CFC; KRAS-specific estimates are limited.

decisions.ocular: involved: persistent ocular dysfunction affects >30% in the usual CFC course; myopia and ptosis support this axis, although KRAS-specific frequencies are uncertain.
